# Twitch (4 endpoints)

## Endpoints

| Resource | Params | Credits | Description |
|----------|--------|---------|-------------|
| /profile | `handle` | 1 | Get Twitch streamer profile |
| /clip | `url` | 1 | Get Twitch clip details |
| /user/videos | `handle` | 1 | List a Twitch user's videos |
| /user/schedule | `handle` | 1 | Get a Twitch user's stream schedule |

### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /profile — 1cr

Returns public profile information for a Twitch streamer including display name, follower count, bio, profile image URL, broadcast language, and partner/affiliate status.

**Parameters**

- `handle`: Twitch username

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/twitch/profile?handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /clip — 1cr

Returns detailed information about a specific Twitch clip including the title, view count, duration, creator name, broadcaster name, game name, thumbnail URL, and creation timestamp.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the Twitch clip

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/twitch/clip?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /user/videos — 1cr

Fetches up to 100 videos for a Twitch user — id, slug, URL, embed URL, title, view count, language, duration in seconds, game info, broadcaster details with follower count, thumbnail URL, and available video qualities.

**Parameters**

- `handle`: Twitch username.
- `filter_by` *(optional)*: Filter the returned videos by type — `HIGHLIGHT` or `UPLOAD`. (Archived past broadcasts are not currently available upstream.)
- `sort_by` *(optional)*: Sort order — `TIME` (newest first) or `VIEWS`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/twitch/user/videos?handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /user/schedule — 1cr

Returns the upcoming stream schedule for a Twitch user — each entry includes start time, end time, title, description, and thumbnail URL.

**Parameters**

- `handle`: Twitch username.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/twitch/user/schedule?handle=<handle>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```


## Choosing a Twitch endpoint

| Your goal | Use this | Credits |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| A streamer's profile | `/profile` | 1 |
| Their past broadcasts / VODs | `/user/videos` | 1 |
| One clip | `/clip` | 1 |
| **When do they actually stream?** | `/user/schedule` | 1 |

All 1 credit, and there is no search — you need the handle up front. Find it elsewhere
(`youtube/search`, `twitter/profile`) and carry it over; streamers usually reuse the handle.

`/user/schedule` (1cr) is the distinctive one: publishing cadence stated by the creator rather
than inferred from timestamps. For any question about how often a competitor shows up, that is
a direct answer instead of an estimate.

## Field Maps


The `profile` endpoint returns an `Author` response normalized by the `twitch-author` field map, and `clip` returns a `Post` normalized by `twitch-post`. Twitch clip responses are nested under `clip.*` upstream; the field map flattens them. Both include computed fields under `data.computed`.
